scope: Proposition 4.1 (Signed pressure law) of the manuscript “Spectral scalar curvature and uniform Urysohn width” (preprints/Spectral-scalar-curvature-and-uniform-Urysohn-width-October-5-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 336 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1b55879b1d10b0f5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every A0, P0, ϵ, b0 > 0, there are constants S0 ∈ (0, 1], T ≥ 10, and a smooth function F : (−S0, S0) × R −→ R that is odd in its first variable and has the following properties. Set N(t) = p t2 + T2, V (t) = N(t)2 = t2 + T2 . (4.1) At every (x, t) ∈ (−S0, S0) × R, Fx ≥ A0N(t), |Ft| ≤ ϵ|F|, FFt ≤ ϵFx, Fx ≤ b0N(t)2 or − FFt ≥ P0Fx, Fx ≤ b0N(t)2 + ϵF2 . (4.2) Moreover, F(x, t) → +∞ as x ↑ S0 and F(x, t) → −∞ as x ↓ −S0, uniformly for t in each compact subset of R.
